newsitem.title: FRANCE: French inflation up Sep after falling for 3 months.
newsitem.headline: French inflation up Sep after falling for 3 months.

text.p: French consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in September after falling for the previous three months, national statistics institute INSEE said on Friday.
Year-on-year, consumer prices rose 1.6 percent, the same as in August and down from 2.0 percent in September 1995.
Economists said the figures were more or less in line with expectations and would have no influence on Bank of France policy in setting interest rates.

The Bank traditionally tracks Bundesbank rate cuts closely keeping a narrow premium over German rates to cushion the franc against any attack by the currency markets, and is very rarely influenced by monthly inflation data.
It has set a goal of keeping inflation below two percent year-on-year.

The September rise followed a monthly drop of 0.3 percent in August, following falls of 0.2 percent in July and 0.1 percent in June, which prompted some politicians to warn of a risk of deflation in the French economy.
But economists said then it was risky to read too much into data skewed by a traditional summer drop in fresh food prices.
The government has said it expects year-on-year inflation of 1.5 percent this year and next.
